messages:
hema: Hey team, filing a quick note about a weird Node SDK streaming quirk I hit while testing auth refresh + AbortController. Repro with the quickstart sample app: if the access token refresh happens mid-stream the client reconnects and we sometimes get interleaved heartbeat comments showing up as empty tokens in the reconstructed text.

noah: Interleaved heartbeat comments? like SSE comments starting with ':'?

hema: Exactly. Raw-ish captured stream (simplified):

```
data: {\"delta\":{\"content\":\"Hel\"}}\n
: ping\n
data: {\"delta\":{\"content\":\"lo\"}}\n
: keepalive\n
data: [DONE]\n
```

When the fetch stream is polyfilled (older node versions) and AbortController abort+reconnect occurs during the comment lines, our parser's line-accumulator can treat the comment as an event delimiter in the wrong spot and produce an extra empty "" token between "Hel" and "lo". On the app side that looks like a spurious blank message.

cory: Huh. Do we attach Last-Event-ID anywhere? That would help server dedupe but not the in-client parse glitch. Which parser function is used in the Node SDK?

hema: The SDK uses a lightweight SSE splitter that splits on "\n\n" and drops lines starting with ':' as comments. The bug happens when a comment line arrives split across buffers: e.g., buffer1 ends with ':' and buffer2 starts with ' ping\n\n' and then the Abort triggers. The splitter ends up emitting an empty data event because it sees the trailing separator in the wrong boundary. Also during auth refresh we immediately start a new fetch and append new chunks to the pending buffer without atomic handoff, which can interleave comment + data from the old + new stream.

noah: So two problems: split-comment handling and non-atomic reconnect swap. Proposed quick fixes?
\
cory: For split comments, treat lines that start with ':' only after fully reconstructing the line (don't drop based on prefix unless newline seen). For reconnect, ensure we pause the consumer while performing reader swap and if any leftover buffer exists, treat EOF as implicit separator (same pattern we've used in other sdks). Also we should log an sse-debug event when we detect comment lines adjacent to data events during reconnect to catch in e2e.

hema: I prototyped a patch: 1) buffer-level line parser that only classifies a line after seeing its newline, 2) during reconnect we call reader.pause(), drain/process leftover, then replace reader and resume. The patch also ignores sole-empty-data events (i.e., events with data:"" after trimming) to avoid surface blank tokens. Local quickstart app passes and the quickstart sample has a --sse-debug flag to dump raw lines.

ci-bot: PR #6789 opened by hema - fix(sdk-node): handle split SSE comment lines and serialize reconnect swaps; drop empty-data events emitted during reconnect. Tests: split-comment simulation + auth-refresh e2e.

noah: Nice. Please add a unit test that simulates: recv() returns ["data: {\"delta\":{\"content\":\"A\"}}\n", ": pi", "ng\n\n", "data: {\"delta\":{\"content\":\"B\"}}\n\n"] and asserts final tokens are ["A","B"]. Also add a quick note in SDK-compat.md about comment handling differences across runtime polyfills.

hema: Added the tests and docs. CI green. Also included a tiny sample showing how to use AbortController gracefully with a short backoff for idempotent clients.

ci-bot: PR #6789 merged to main by cory - changelog: fix(sdk-node): correct split-comment parsing and make reconnect atomic to prevent empty tokens during auth refresh; add tests + docs + sample

hema: Verified staging with the sample app doing 100 rapid auth-refresh cycles. No empty tokens observed. Marking this resolved for now. Will follow up if QA sees anything else.
